entries.title: Joshua 7:1
segments:
The children of Israel; Israel is regarded as constituting one people consecrated to God's service; and the sin of a single member pollutes the whole body, and brings it under God's displeasure. 
 
Sins known only to those who commit them and to God may occasion calamities to a nation, and be the means of bringing many to an untimely grave.

entries.title: Joshua 7:2
segments: Ai; a city north-west of Jericho; the same as Hai.

entries.title: Joshua 7:3
segments: Great prosperity often tempts men to be self-confident, and leads them to neglect those means which are essential to their continued success.

entries.title: Joshua 7:4
segments: When men undertake plans in reliance on their own judgment or that of others, without inquiring of God, or seeking his direction, they will be likely to fail, and instead of success meet with speedy and sore disappointment.

entries.title: Joshua 7:5
segments:
Became as water; were utterly discouraged. 
 
Men are prone to go to extremes, and after being highly elated, to sink into despair.

entries.title: Joshua 7:6
segments: Put dust upon their heads; in token of deep distress.

entries.title: Joshua 7:7
segments: In trouble we should humble ourselves on account of our sins, and implore pardoning mercy; especially inquiring why it is that God contendeth with us, and seeking to know his will, that we may do it.

entries.title: Joshua 7:9
segments:
What wilt thou do? how would God secure his honor as faithful to his promises and able to fulfil them. 
 
When we truly desire the honor of God, and wish for success in our efforts that he may be glorified, our prayers will be accepted and answered in rich mercy.

entries.title: Joshua 7:11
segments: The cause of all trouble is sin; and so long as it is indulged, however secretly, we cannot expect deliverance, or the protection and blessing of God.

entries.title: Joshua 7:13
segments: All iniquity is perfectly known to God, and it is a solemn thing to stand before him and have it brought to light and spread out before the sun.

entries.title: Joshua 7:14
segments: The Lord taketh; designates by lot as presently explained.

entries.title: Joshua 7:15
segments: The punishment which God sometimes brings upon the workers of iniquity here, is a premonition of the more dreadful woes which will come upon them hereafter.

entries.title: Joshua 7:18
segments: The idea of keeping sin a secret is vain: those who commit it may be sure that, sooner or later, their sin will find them out.

entries.title: Joshua 7:19
segments: Give--glory to the Lord; by confessing the truth.

entries.title: Joshua 7:21
segments: I saw, I coveted, and I took, describes the course with regard to forbidden objects, of multitudes of transgressors; and their condition, when their sins are brought to light, is in total contrast to what they expected when they committed them.

entries.title: Joshua 7:24
segments: His sons, and his daughters; the lives of all are at God's disposal, and he has an absolute right to take them when and how he pleases.  In the present case he saw good to direct that all Achan's family, as well as his possessions, should perish with him.  We may reasonably suppose that one design of this was to impress more deeply upon the minds of the Israelites the malignant nature of sin, and its tendency to involve in ruin not only the transgressor himself, but all connected with him.  For the administration of justice by human judges he gave a different rule: "The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin."

entries.title: Joshua 7:25
segments: There are cases where God requires transgressors to be put to death, and his anger will not be turned away from a people unless they execute this punishment.
